title: Predictive Engagement
summary: Website journeys, segments, action maps, Messenger, and the Journey Outcomes deprecation. This is not ACD predictive routing.

lessons.title: Predictive Engagement watches the site, not the queue math
lessons.summary: It predicts what a visitor is trying to do and offers a message, a chat, content, or a flow. Predictive routing is a different feature on the queue.
paras: The About Predictive Engagement page calls it a Genesys Cloud AI feature that analyzes how visitors behave on websites, predicts the outcomes they are trying to reach, and personalizes the engagement. The use-case page says it uses machine learning, segmentation, and real-time outcome scoring, then engages with chat, a chatbot, or a content offer. You can also hand the moment to an Architect flow. None of that is the ACD routing method named predictive routing.

Agents later see journey information on the interaction. Supervisors get visitor activity and action-map performance. Those reports sit beside contact-center analytics. They do not replace service level on the queue. Read the deprecation notice before you design anything that depends on Journey Outcomes. That feature has a planned end.

lessons.title: Messenger tracks web messaging. The old snippet tracks web chat.
lessons.summary: Genesys tells Genesys Cloud CX customers to use web messaging. Leaving both snippets on the page double-counts the visit.
paras: The about page says you can use web messaging with Predictive Engagement and encourages web messaging instead of web chat. The tracking-snippet article is explicit: web chat deploys the Predictive Engagement tracking snippet; web messaging deploys the Messenger snippet. Paste a tracking snippet in the head of the main window, not in an iframe. After ac('init') on a traditional snippet, or ac('load') on the SPA snippet, Predictive Engagement tracks pageview events.

The migration article tells you to remove the tracking snippet when you deploy Messenger, because Digital User Tracking is already part of Messenger and two snippets double-track. Enable Digital User Tracking on the Messenger configuration, publish a new version, and point action maps that still say web chat at web messaging. The Messenger article says to turn on the Predictive Engagement toggle in the Apps tab when you want journey data, then use Live Now to see events.

lessons.title: A segment matches visitors who meet every condition you listed
lessons.summary: At least one condition. More conditions, fewer visitors. Conditions are not shared with the next segment.
paras: The use case describes a segment as a way to categorize visitors by shared behavior and attributes. Attributes it gives as examples include browser, device, location, campaign, and referrer. That list is not a schema. The best-practices page says a segment needs at least one condition, that you should design the conditions for a specific action map, and that adding conditions reduces how many visitors match. Conditions are not shared across segments and outcomes.

The same best-practices page carries the Journey Outcomes deprecation banner. A segment that exists only to feed an outcome trigger is on borrowed time. Build the segment for a visitor you can still recognize from attributes and activity after outcomes stop qualifying action maps.

lessons.title: An action map is qualified before it is offered
lessons.summary: Segment, visitor activity, and outcome probability are the trigger kinds. Priority breaks a tie. Web chat is the legacy action.
paras: Creating an action map starts with a name and an action: web messaging, web chat, a content offer, or an advanced orchestration flow. You then set what triggers it. The create page names segment, visitor activity, and outcome. The triggers article is the page that defines those rules, including outcome probability. The overview says a qualified map may still be held back by other offer conditions, and that priority decides which map is offered when several qualify. Web offers can be limited to particular pages.

For a web chat or web messaging offer you can pick an agent queue, and a schedule group so the offer appears only when agents are available. You can override the global frequency cap for one map. The overview’s advice about waiting for a drop in outcome score is tied to Journey Outcomes. Treat that advice as historical design, and read the deprecation before you make outcome probability the only trigger.

lessons.title: Journey Outcomes have a published end date
lessons.summary: Announced 18 May 2026. Planned effective date 29 June 2026. Outcome scoring is not part of the Customer Outcomes replacement.
paras: The deprecation announcement lists the announced date as 2026-05-18 and the planned effective date as 2026-06-29. After that date the page says customers cannot create or manage outcomes, existing outcomes are not processed, new outcome records are not generated, outcomes do not trigger action maps, and outcome reporting is not available. Action maps that have only an outcome trigger stop qualifying. The map is not deleted. The trigger is removed. Architect flows that call getJourneyOutcome skip that branch and otherwise run.

Customer Outcomes is described as a new platform feature under development. It is a simpler event model. The announcement says outcome scoring will not be part of it. A different announcement says a future Predictive Routing framework will take customer-defined business outcomes, including metrics that live outside Genesys Cloud, and that existing predictive-routing configurations need no change until you migrate. This lab read both pages on 15 October 2026, after the planned Journey Outcomes date. It did not sign in to an organization. If either page has moved, the page wins.
lessons.uncertainty: Read on 15 October 2026. The planned effective date on the announcement was 2026-06-29. This lab did not confirm the state of a live organization. Customer Outcomes was still described as under development. The Predictive Routing custom-outcome framework was described as a future release.

lessons.title: An Architect flow can be the action, and it can also be the thing you must edit
lessons.summary: Advanced orchestration is an action type. Flows that still call getJourneyOutcome need a path that does not depend on it.
paras: The about page lists Architect workflows and Architect flow actions as the way to integrate Predictive Engagement with other systems, including a listed topic for Salesforce lead creation and campaign attribution. This lab does not restate Salesforce fields. The create page names advanced orchestration flow as one of the four action types, beside web messaging, web chat, and a content offer.

If that flow asks Journey Outcomes for a score, the deprecation page says the getJourneyOutcome branch is skipped and the flow otherwise runs. Give the visitor a next step that does not need the score: a queue, a content offer, or a segment-based map. The Salesforce topic on the about page is an integration you open in the resource center, not a screen this lab redraws from memory.

lessons.title: Prove the map with Live Now and the performance reports
lessons.summary: Visitor activity and action-map performance are the Predictive Engagement reports. Outcome columns age out with the deprecation.
paras: The about page points supervisors at live visitor tracking, visitor activity, and action-map performance, and at journey columns on Genesys Cloud performance views. The use case describes visitor activity by device, segments matched, outcomes achieved, and action-map performance for web chat, content offers, and Architect flow. Use those reports to see whether a map fired. Use Live Now when you are still proving that the snippet sees the page.

Outcomes achieved will not stay a trustworthy column through the deprecation. The announcement tells you to export outcome reports you need before the effective date. After that, judge the map by segments, activity, and the offers visitors actually got. A quiet report can mean the snippet is missing, the segment is too narrow, the frequency cap held the offer, or the schedule group hid it because nobody was On Queue.
lessons.uncertainty: The use case names action types web chat, content offers, and Architect flow. It does not, in the section this lab used, name a web-messaging column. Confirm that column on the report before you tell someone it is missing.
